chunks: And ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Yazīd ibn ‘Abdil Malik, who said:

I was with Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when a group of people passed by riding on donkeys. He asked me, 'Where are these people going?' I replied, 'To the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'What prevents them from going to the Ziyārah of the lonely (abandoned) Martyr?'
One of the people from Iraq asked him, 'Is his Ziyārah obligatory?'
He said, 'His Ziyārah is better than one Hajj and one ‘Umrah, and another ‘Umrah and another Hajj,' until he counted twenty Hajjs and twenty ‘Umrahs, purified and accepted.
Yazīd said: I swear to Allāh, I did not leave until a man came to him and said, 'I have performed Hajj nineteen times. Please pray to Allāh that He grants me the completion of the twentieth.'
He asked, 'Have you visited al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' The man replied, 'No.' He said, 'Verily, his Ziyārah is better than twenty Hajjs.'

key_terms.الْغَرِيبِ الشَّهِيدِ: Al-Gharīb al-Shahīd (The Lonely/Abandoned Martyr, a title for Imam al-Ḥusayn)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of visiting Imam al-Husain compared to Hajj according to Kamil al-Ziyarat?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Ṣādiq’s (a.s.) critique of the general practice of visiting various martyrs' graves while neglecting the preeminent shrine of al-Ḥusayn (a.s.), whom he designates as the 'Gharīb al-Shahīd' (Lonely Martyr). This hadith establishes the theological principle that Ziyārah to al-Ḥusayn holds superior merit to multiple Hajjs and ‘Umrahs, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence to emphasize the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in spiritual devotion. The narrative further illustrates the cumulative reward structure, where the man’s request for the 'twentieth' Hajj underscores the belief that Ziyārah completes and perfects one's obligatory acts of worship.
